An alternate form of '''Aurebesh numerals''' was used in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Completely different from regular [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]], the numbers were used on the excursion vehicle ''[[Dustskimmer]]'', in [[Transponder code/Legends|transponder code]] profiles for [[Starship/Legends|starships]], on a [[Map/Legends|map]] of destinations on the [[Subtram/Legends|subtram]] in the [[Coruscant Underworld/Legends|Coruscant underworld]], on [[Credit ingot/Legends|credit ingots]], and on certain galactic [[Map/Legends|maps]].

==Description==
The numerals were completely different from regular [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]] numbers, using an alternate numerical system based on dots and lines, with numerals for 0 through 16 being represented.<ref name="Platt">''[[Platt's Starport Guide]]''</ref>

==History==
[[File:1stClassSign-KOTOR37.png|thumb|left|200px|"1st class"]]
These numbers were known to be used in [[Transponder code/Legends|transponder code]] profiles for [[Starship/Legends|starships]],<ref name="Platt" /> and on some [[Map/Legends|maps]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="Jedi Knight">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref>

In approximately [[3963 BBY]], a sign over an entrance to the excursion vehicle ''[[Dustskimmer]]'' on [[Metellos 3]] said "1ST CLASS", with the number 1 written in this font.<ref name="KOTOR37" />

During the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]], an enlistment propaganda poster in the [[Justicar territory|Justicar sector]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] used alternative numerals and stated that "failure to register may result in a fee of up to 2000{{Cr}} or incarceration".<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref>  

At the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], alternative numerals were engraved on [[Credit ingot/Legends|credit ingots]] used by a band of [[Moogan/Legends|Moogan]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] to bribe a [[Unidentified Mandalorian customs official/Legends|corrupt customs officer]] on [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]. The [[Color/Legends|silvery]] ingots read "8 88," while the golden ones said "{{Cr}}84."<ref name="Corruption">{{TCW|Corruption (episode)}}</ref> 

They also appeared on a map of destinations on the [[Subtram/Legends|subtram]] in the [[Coruscant Underworld/Legends|Coruscant underworld]].<ref name="Trivia" />

The hull of the modified [[TIE Advanced x1/Legends|TIE Advanced x1]] known as ''[[Calrissian Runner]]'' featured [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]] text, with the numerals displayed in this typeface: "WS 2", "PN 8", "SI GN 06" and "IBR 54".<ref name="Running the Belt">{{GamerCite|9|Running the Belt}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I can't recall which came first, Stock Ships or Gamemaster Screen Revised, but I worked on both and both have that chart.|[[Pablo Hidalgo]] on [[Wikipedia:Twitter|Twitter]]|<ref name="Hidalgo New Aurabesh">{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|status/1535405496089186307|[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|date=2022-06-10|quote=I can't recall which came first, Stock Ships or Gamemaster Screen Revised, but I worked on both and both have that chart.}}</ref>}}
[[File:Subtram_map.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A subtram map created for "To Catch a Jedi," using alternate Aurebesh numerals]]
This alternate numerical system first appeared in a graphic called "Current [[Transponder code/Legends|transponder code]] profile" in ''[[Platt's Starport Guide]]'', a supplement to the [[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game|''Star Wars'' roleplaying game]] by [[West End Games]], published in [[February]] [[1995]].<ref name="Platt" /> The same graph subsequently appeared in the roleplaying supplements ''[[Star Wars Gamemaster Screen, Revised]]''<ref name="Screen">''[[Star Wars Gamemaster Screen, Revised]]''</ref> and ''[[Stock Ships]]''.<ref name="Stock">''[[Stock Ships]]''</ref>

The alternate numerals also appear on a map of destinations on the [[Subtram/Legends|subtram]] in the [[Coruscant Underworld/Legends|Coruscant Underworld]], created for the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' episode "[[To Catch a Jedi]]."<ref name="Trivia" /> However, although the map does appear on-screen in the episode, it is too far away to decipher.<ref name="Catch">{{TCW|To Catch a Jedi}}</ref>
